subject.title: Auto-apply safe doctor fixes on gateway start

question: Should Gateway startup ever apply doctor repairs to persistent config automatically, and if so should that be default-on or an explicit opt-in safe-repair subset?
rationale: Current source, docs, and tests intentionally keep Gateway startup from rewriting config, while the issue asks to change persistent state during a security- and channel-sensitive startup path.

options.title: Keep startup read-only
options.body: Leave Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, and improve doctor logging or narrower repair issues instead of mutating config during startup.

options.title: Add opt-in safe startup repair
options.body: Define a small repair allowlist with logged diffs and tests for upgrade, security, provider, and channel behavior before enabling it behind a config or setup choice.

options.title: Auto-apply safe repairs by default
options.body: Make startup self-heal legacy config automatically, accepting the upgrade and security risk only after explicit maintainer sponsorship and broad proof.

recommendation.title: Keep startup read-only
recommendation.body: Leave Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, and improve doctor logging or narrower repair issues instead of mutating config during startup.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` owns the most recent current-line edits on the startup validation and doctor-doc surface, making him the best available routing candidate for the product-policy choice.
